finding.expected: Close F1 completely. A synchronization path must not return after a recoverable synchronization/restoration failure while branch, HEAD, index, or worktree differ from the exact pre-sync state. Regression coverage must inject restoration-stage failure and prove the exact pre-sync HEAD/branch, clean status, original tracked-file contents, absence of upstream-only files, no RUN creation, and no Executor invocation. Do not weaken TASK-062 by redefining fail-closed as error-reporting only. If exact preservation cannot be established under the existing TASK constraints, surface that as BLOCKED rather than claiming semantic completion.
finding.issue: The remediation now surfaces rollback failures instead of swallowing them, but it still does not establish the required exact pre-sync repository state when a restoration command itself fails. In the read-tree restoration-failure regression, forward read-tree has already changed index/worktree state and the forced rollback read-tree failure leaves that mutation unrecovered. In the update-ref restoration- failure regression, a forced ref rollback failure can leave HEAD at upstream while index/worktree are restored toward local. Both tests assert only explicit failure, no RUN creation, and no Executor invocation; they do not assert restored HEAD, branch, cleanliness, file contents, or absence of upstream-only files. F1 therefore remains unresolved against TASK-062's fail-closed exact pre-sync-state invariant.
